1:# Work Leaf Architecture
2:
3:This document describes the stable architecture and extension boundaries for Work Leaf. Code changes
4:should preserve these boundaries unless a human explicitly authorizes an architecture change.
5:
6:## Public Crate Surface
7:
8:`src/lib.rs` is the public crate index. It exposes the modules that external callers, tests, UIs, and
9:agent-provider integrations use:
10:
11:- `agent` and `agent_runtime` define provider-neutral agent domain types and runtime contracts.
12:- `workspace` defines the UI-neutral controller and DTOs used by frontends.
13:- `cli` defines the command-chat API used by the binary and by controller orchestration.
14:- `codex` defines the Codex provider implementation.
15:- `http_controller` defines the localhost HTTP transport used by the daemon and CLI process
16:  boundary.
17:- `orchestrator`, `patch`, `review`, `linearize`, and `locks` define core workflow behavior.
18:- `terminal_app`, `ui`, and `ui_harness` define the terminal frontend and terminal-specific tests.
19:
20:Public re-exports in `src/lib.rs` are part of the supported integration surface. The most important
21:public interfaces are:
22:
23:- UI integration: `WorkLeafController`, `WorkLeafSnapshot`, `WorkLeafSession`, `WorkLeafEvent`,
24:  `WorkLeafLoading`.
25:- Agent-provider integration: `AgentBackend`, `AgentStreamEvent`, `AgentShutdownHandle`,
26:  `AgentProfile`, `AgentKind`, `AgentLaunch`, `AgentSession`, `AgentId`, `ChatMessage`,
27:  `MessageRole`, `PromptPolicy`, `ReadPermission`, `AgentError`.
28:- Command orchestration: `CommandChat`, `CommandChatResult`, `ProcessCommand`, `CliError`.
29:- Localhost controller transport: `HttpControllerClient`, `HttpControllerServer`,
30:  `OrchestratorHttpError`.
31:- Core workflows: `AgentOrchestrator`, `GitPatcher`, `PatchCoordinator`, `GitHistory`,
32:  `ReviewCoordinator`, `LinearizePlanner`, `FileLockTable`.
33:- Terminal UI: `TerminalApp`, `RemoteTerminalApp`, `TerminalUi`, `UiHarness`, `UiAction`, `UiKey`,
34:  `UiMode`, `UiSurface`, `PaneFocus`, `AgentListEntry`.
35:
36:## Layering
37:
38:The application is organized as four layers.
39:
40:1. Provider-neutral domain and runtime contracts live in `src/agent.rs` and
41:   `src/agent_runtime.rs`.
42:2. Core workflows live in `src/cli.rs`, `src/orchestrator.rs`, `src/patch.rs`, `src/review.rs`,
43:   `src/linearize.rs`, and `src/locks.rs`.
44:3. The UI-neutral application controller lives in `src/workspace.rs`.
45:4. Frontend adapters live in `src/terminal_app.rs`, `src/ui.rs`, and `src/ui_harness.rs`.
46:
47:The dependency direction is inward. UIs drive `WorkLeafController`; the controller drives
48:`CommandChat`; `CommandChat` drives the active `AgentBackend` and the workflow coordinators. Core
49:workflow modules do not depend on terminal rendering, terminal input, or a specific agent provider.
50:
51:The package has two binary targets. `src/bin/work-leaf-orchestrator.rs` calls
52:`work_leaf::run_orchestrator_from_env()`, creates the Codex backend and `CommandChat`, wraps them in
53:`WorkLeafController<CodexBackend>`, and exposes that controller through
54:`src/http_controller.rs::HttpControllerServer` on a localhost HTTP address. The daemon prints a
55:machine-readable `WORK_LEAF_ORCHESTRATOR_URL=http://...` startup line after binding.
56:
57:`src/bin/work-leaf.rs` calls `work_leaf::run_cli_from_env()`. The CLI connects to
58:`WORK_LEAF_ORCHESTRATOR_URL` when that environment variable is present; otherwise it starts the
59:sibling `work-leaf-orchestrator` binary on `127.0.0.1:0`, reads the printed URL, and connects to that
60:daemon. A CLI-managed daemon receives `WORK_LEAF_PARENT_PID`, does not inherit the terminal file
61:descriptors, and exits when that parent process is gone. The terminal frontend renders through
62:`src/terminal_app.rs::RemoteTerminalApp`, which drives `src/http_controller.rs::HttpControllerClient`.
63:The in-process `src/terminal_app.rs::TerminalApp<B>` remains the local controller adapter used by
64:tests and embedders that construct a `CommandChat<B>` directly.
65:
66:The project-root `start` script builds both binary targets in release mode, starts
67:`work-leaf-orchestrator` on `127.0.0.1:7878` by default, exports the printed URL for `work-leaf`,
68:and terminates the daemon when the CLI process exits. `WORK_LEAF_START_LISTEN` selects a different
69:listen address when a caller needs an explicit override; the script does not fall back to another
70:port when the requested address is unavailable.
71:
72:## Agent Domain
73:
74:`src/agent.rs` owns provider-neutral agent data:
75:
76:- `AgentId` validates stable agent identifiers.
77:- `AgentKind` identifies the provider kind. `AgentKind::Codex` is the built-in provider, and
78:  `AgentKind::External(String)` identifies non-Codex providers.
79:- `AgentProfile` carries the active provider kind, display name, and default feature label.
80:- `AgentLaunch` describes a new agent session request.
81:- `AgentSession` stores the agent id, kind, feature, state, messages, and modified files.
82:- `ChatMessage` and `MessageRole` model conversation history.
83:- `PromptPolicy` injects project instructions and worktree access rules into agent prompts.
84:- `ReadPermission` selects whether prompts require orchestrator-mediated reads or allow direct
85:  filesystem reads while keeping writes mediated by patches.
86:- `AgentError` is the shared error type for launch, send, and prompt policy failures.
87:
88:`src/agent.rs` also re-exports `AgentBackend`, `AgentStreamEvent`, and `AgentShutdownHandle` from
89:`src/agent_runtime.rs`, so callers can import all provider-neutral agent interfaces from
90:`work_leaf::agent`.
91:
92:## Agent Runtime Interface
93:
94:`src/agent_runtime.rs` owns the provider-neutral backend contract:
95:
96:- `AgentBackend::launch` starts an agent session from an `AgentLaunch`.
97:- `AgentBackend::send` sends a prompt to an existing agent session.
98:- `AgentBackend::launch_streaming` and `AgentBackend::send_streaming` provide real-time output to a
99:  sink of `AgentStreamEvent` values. Their default implementations call the non-streaming methods.
100:- `AgentBackend::shutdown_handle` returns an `AgentShutdownHandle` for terminating active provider
101:  processes.
102:- `AgentStreamEvent` carries status text, streamed agent messages, and streamed errors.
103:- `AgentShutdownHandle::shutdown` terminates registered processes, waits briefly, and then kills
104:  remaining processes.
105:
106:The runtime also contains provider-process support that is not part of the public provider API:
107:registered child processes are tracked in an internal registry; Unix children run in their own
108:process group; Linux children receive a parent-death signal; shutdown first sends terminate and then
109:kill to remaining processes. This behavior is used by provider implementations that spawn real
110:processes.
111:
112:New agent providers implement `AgentBackend`; they do not add provider logic to `src/codex.rs`.
113:Providers that need real-time UI output should override the streaming methods. Providers implemented
114:inside this crate can use the crate-private process registration helpers for shared shutdown.
115:Providers outside this crate can implement launch, send, and streaming through the public trait; a
116:public lifecycle extension is required before external child processes can participate in the shared
117:`AgentShutdownHandle` registry.
118:
119:## Codex Provider
120:
121:`src/codex.rs` contains the Codex-specific implementation of the neutral agent runtime interface:
122:
123:- `SandboxMode` and `CodexCommandConfig` define Codex CLI invocation settings.
124:- `CodexInvocation` records the command, arguments, and prompt used for an invocation.
125:- `CodexBackend` stores Codex session history and implements `AgentBackend`.
126:- `CodexBackend::build_launch_invocation` and `CodexBackend::build_send_invocation` construct
127:  `codex exec` and `codex exec resume` calls. Launch invocations include the injected
128:  `PromptPolicy`; resumed invocations for known sessions pass only the follow-up message because the
129:  Codex thread already contains the launch-time policy and repository instructions.
130:- `CodexBackend::record_launch_reply`, `record_launch_output`, and `session` maintain in-memory
131:  session state.
132:- `CodexBackend` parses Codex `--json` event lines from stdout to capture `thread.started`
133:  identifiers for resume and to convert agent message, error, and status events into
134:  `AgentStreamEvent` values. The parser accepts standard JSON whitespace around field separators
135:  while preserving string contents.
136:
137:`CodexBackend` is a provider implementation, not the owner of the generic agent contract. Callers
138:that need provider-neutral behavior import `AgentBackend` from `work_leaf::agent` or from the
139:top-level re-export, not from `work_leaf::codex`.
140:
141:## Command Chat
142:
143:`src/cli.rs::CommandChat<B>` is the command orchestration surface shared by the CLI, controller, and
144:tests. It is generic over `B: AgentBackend`.
145:
146:`CommandChat` owns:
147:
148:- project root and prompt policy,
149:- active `AgentProfile`,
150:- agent sessions and generated agent ids,
151:- orchestrator, patch, review, and linearizer coordination,
152:- transcript output for command-mode and UI consumers,
153:- backend shutdown through `AgentShutdownHandle`.
154:
155:The primary public methods are:
156:
157:- `CommandChat::new` for constructing command chat state with a backend.
158:- `CommandChat::with_agent_profile` for selecting a non-default provider profile.
159:- `CommandChat::handle_line` for processing command lines such as `new`, `chat`, `review`, and
160:  `linearize`.
161:- `CommandChat::prepare_agent_launch`, `launch_prepared_agent_streaming`, and
162:  `launch_prepared_agent_streaming_with_ids` for UI-driven launch flows.
163:- `CommandChat::send_to_agent`, `send_to_agent_streaming`, and
164:  `send_to_agent_streaming_with_ids` for UI-driven message flows.
165:- `CommandChat::shutdown_agents` and `shutdown_handle` for lifecycle cleanup.
166:
167:`CommandChat` uses the active `AgentProfile` when launching user agents, reviewers, and linearizers.
168:Workflow code must not hard-code `AgentKind::Codex` when the active profile supplies the provider.
169:
170:## UI-Neutral Controller
171:
172:`src/workspace.rs::WorkLeafController<B>` is the preferred API for frontends. It owns UI-neutral
173:application state and hides worker management from frontend adapters.
174:
175:The controller owns:
176:
177:- session selection and session snapshots,
178:- per-session loading state,
179:- LLM-generated chat titles through hidden `title-<agent-id>` backend launches, with
180:  `src/chat_title.rs::ChatTitleAgent` tracking first-prompt naming state,
181:- command transcripts,
182:- background launch/send/review workers,
183:- stream routing from `AgentStreamEvent` into the selected session,
184:- review startup, automatic per-patch-agent review routing, reviewer-session creation, and
185:  reviewed-commit bookkeeping,
186:- shutdown propagation to running agents.
187:
188:When an agent worker finishes, the controller records the agent output and clears that session's
189:loading state. A user-agent response becomes review-ready only when the orchestrator transcript shows
190:an applied patch from that agent and the agent emits `@work-leaf done`. Successful patch application
191:returns a continuation prompt to the patch agent when the agent has not reported done, so the agent can
192:run repository-required checks through locked command directives, provide follow-up patches, or signal
193:review readiness. Repository build, test, format, and required-check commands run only through
194:agent-emitted orchestrator directives that name the command and the write-lock paths the command may
195:touch. Locked command runs have a five-minute default timeout, after which the command is terminated,
196:locks are released, and a longer run requires user authorization. `PromptPolicy` injects project
197:instruction files into agent prompts, and the active backend agent is responsible for choosing and
198:requesting the repository checks required by those instructions before reporting work done.
199:Tracked file changes produced by locked commands remain pending for that patch agent until the agent
200:commits them through the patch protocol or reverts them. Pending command changes block
201:`@work-leaf done`, and the orchestrator returns the tracked diff so the agent can submit the command
202:output as a provisional patch when it belongs in the final work.
203:
204:Review bookkeeping has three scopes. The controller records a launch-time review baseline for each
205:patch agent, tracks the latest reviewed hash for that patch agent so the same agent head is not
206:reviewed twice, and asks reviewers to inspect every provisional commit from the active baseline
207:through the latest patch-agent commit. `CommandChat` also keeps the ordered exact review targets that
208:completed review during the active instance, and those targets form the linearizer handoff. This lets
209:one patch-agent session complete more than one reviewed patch without a later hash replacing earlier
210:reviewed work in the linearizer prompt.
211:
212:The command transcript is also the conversation history for the persistent `command-agent`. That
213:system agent interprets chat sent to the Work Leaf command surface. It recognizes literal command
214:lines and common natural-language requests for help, review, linearization, quitting, and launching
215:one or more user agents. Multi-agent launch requests dispatch `new [prompt...]` once per requested
216:agent through the same controller paths used by command-mode input.
217:
218:Frontend code should use these methods:
219:
220:- `WorkLeafController::new` to wrap a `CommandChat<B>`.
221:- `snapshot` to read renderable state.
222:- `drain_events` to consume UI-neutral events.
223:- `execute_command_line` to run command-mode input.
224:- `create_agent` to reserve, select, and launch an agent session from a prompt.
225:- `send_command_agent_message` to route chat from the Work Leaf command surface to `command-agent`.
226:- `send_message` to send a prompt to one session while other sessions may still be busy.
227:- `start_review` to create or resume reviewer sessions for explicit history-wide review and stream
228:  reviewer output.
229:- `is_busy`, `wait_for_idle`, and `wait_for_session_line` for tests and event loops.
230:- `shutdown` to terminate active backend processes.
231:
232:The controller exposes renderable state through:
233:
234:- `WorkLeafSnapshot`, which contains the command transcript and sessions.
235:- `WorkLeafSession`, which contains agent id, kind, feature/title, transcript lines, and loading
236:  state.
237:- `WorkLeafEvent`, which reports session creation, session updates, streamed lines, selection
238:  changes, transcript lines, and quit requests.
239:- `WorkLeafLoading`, which distinguishes launch and waiting-for-reply states.
240:
241:`WorkLeafEvent` uses append-oriented transcript events for efficient remote frontends. `AgentAdded`
242:provides the initial session snapshot, `AgentLineAppended` carries one new session line, and
243:`CommandTranscriptLine` carries one new command transcript line. `AgentStatusUpdated` carries
244:session metadata and loading state without re-sending the session transcript. `AgentUpdated` remains
245:part of the DTO surface for full-session replacement when an integration needs it. Session line
246:appends and status changes are not paired with full-session replacement events, so remote frontends
247:can update long transcripts without re-receiving the full transcript text.
248:
249:New UIs should consume `WorkLeafController` and these DTOs. They should not duplicate worker
250:spawning, session naming, review lookup, loading bookkeeping, or orchestrator event routing.
251:
252:## Localhost HTTP Controller
253:
254:`src/http_controller.rs::HttpControllerServer` is a transport adapter over `WorkLeafController`. It
255:owns no workflow behavior; each HTTP route delegates to the corresponding controller method or DTO:
256:
257:- `GET /snapshot` returns `WorkLeafSnapshot`.
258:- `POST /events/drain` returns pending `WorkLeafEvent` values after polling workers when needed.
259:- `GET /busy` returns the controller busy state.
260:- `POST /command` calls `WorkLeafController::execute_command_line`.
261:- `POST /command-agent` calls `WorkLeafController::send_command_agent_message`.
262:- `POST /agent/message` calls `WorkLeafController::send_message`.
263:- `POST /agent/interrupt` calls `WorkLeafController::interrupt_agent`.
264:- `POST /transcript` calls `WorkLeafController::push_transcript_line`.
265:- `POST /loading-text` calls `WorkLeafController::loading_text`.
266:- `POST /shutdown` calls `WorkLeafController::shutdown` and stops the daemon loop.
267:
268:`src/http_controller.rs::HttpControllerClient` is the matching blocking localhost client. It
269:serializes and deserializes the same workspace DTOs used by in-process frontends. `AgentId`
270:deserialization uses `src/agent.rs::AgentId::new`, so HTTP payloads preserve the same identifier
271:validation as local controller calls.
272:
273:## Terminal UI
274:
275:The terminal frontend is an adapter over the UI-neutral controller surface.
276:
277:`src/terminal_app.rs::TerminalApp<B>` translates raw terminal bytes and modal editing state into
278:direct `WorkLeafController<B>` calls for in-process use. `src/terminal_app.rs::RemoteTerminalApp`
279:uses the same terminal state machine with `HttpControllerClient` for the CLI/daemon process split.
280:Both adapters keep a local render snapshot, apply `WorkLeafEvent` values to that cache and to
281:`TerminalUi`, and render from the cache rather than fetching a full controller snapshot for every
282:frame. They own terminal event-loop concerns such as insert mode, prompt mode, `Ctrl-W` navigation,
283:SGR mouse clicks, SGR mouse wheel scrolling of the right pane, chunked terminal input parsing,
284:rendering invalidation, and polling background workers. Insert mode sends chat text to the selected
285:agent session, or to `command-agent` when the Work Leaf command surface is selected. Bracketed-paste
286:newlines and Shift+Enter are chat prompt line breaks. A plain Enter submits the buffered chat text.
287:When an agent chat is selected in command mode, `/` focuses the chat, seeds the chat buffer with
288:`/`, and enters insert mode so `/status`-style input submits through the same selected-agent chat
289:path.
290:
291:The terminal app maps a session to a left-pane `READY` marker when the controller exposes no loading
292:state for that session. `TerminalUi` queues one terminal bell when a chat transitions into the ready
293:state and renders ready rows in reverse video so they remain highlighted until the chat becomes busy
294:again.
295:
296:`src/ui.rs::TerminalUi` owns terminal-specific presentation state:
297:
298:- `UiMode`, `PaneFocus`, `UiSurface`, `UiKey`, and `UiAction` model terminal interactions.
299:- `AgentListEntry` is the terminal left-pane representation of an agent row.
300:- `TerminalLayout` computes pane geometry.
301:- `TerminalUi` renders left/right panes, prompts, cursor placement, command-interface selection, and
302:  terminal navigation actions. The right pane keeps the chat prompt visible while scroll offsets
303:  reveal earlier transcript rows.
304:
305:`src/ui_harness.rs::UiHarness` is the test harness for terminal behavior. It exercises the same
306:`TerminalUi` frame path used by the interactive example. UI tests should drive
307:`UiHarness::handle_byte` or `UiHarness::handle_bytes` rather than duplicating terminal input logic.
308:
309:A web UI, desktop UI, or non-terminal integration should not depend on `TerminalApp` or
310:`TerminalUi`; it should depend on `WorkLeafController` and the DTOs in `src/workspace.rs`.
311:
312:## Core Workflow Modules
313:
314:`src/orchestrator.rs::AgentOrchestrator<B>` parses and executes `@work-leaf` directives emitted by
315:agents. It uses `FileLockTable` for file reads and command write locks, `CommandWritePolicy` for
316:command classification, `PatchCoordinator` for patch requests, and the active `AgentBackend` for
317:routed follow-up messages. Its public output is `OrchestratorEvent`.
318:
319:`src/locks.rs::FileLockTable` owns root-scoped path normalization and read/write locking.
320:`FileSnapshot` carries file read results. `CommandWritePolicy` and `CommandWriteIntent` provide
321:heuristic read-only/write-intent classification for commands when an agent is unsure. Agent-requested
322:command runs execute in the project root while `FileLockTable` holds write locks for the normalized
323:lock paths supplied by the agent. File paths are normalized relative to the project root and cannot
324:escape that root.
325:
326:`src/patch.rs::GitPatcher` validates and applies unified diffs under write locks and creates
327:metadata commits for accepted patches. It also accepts a matching already-applied diff when a locked
328:command has produced the tracked working-tree change, so the command output can be saved as the
329:agent's provisional patch. `PatchCoordinator<B>` connects patch conflicts and malformed patch
330:diagnostics back to the active agent backend. `PatchRequest`, `PatchOutcome`, and `PatchError` are
331:the public patch workflow types.
332:
333:`src/review.rs::GitHistory` reads latest agent commits from repository history, builds cumulative
334:review targets for a patch agent since a launch or reviewed baseline, and resolves agent metadata
335:commits by exact hash. `ReviewCoordinator<B>` launches reviewer agents against those review targets
336:and loops until the reviewer reports no findings or the configured maximum round count is reached.
337:`CommandChat` resolves reviewer `@work-leaf` directives, such as file reads, before interpreting
338:reviewer output as findings. `CommandChat` and `WorkLeafController` keep a stable
339:`review-<agent-id>` reviewer identity for each patch agent and skip latest agent heads that have
340:already completed review. `AgentCommit`, `ReviewResult`, and `ReviewError` are the public review
341:workflow types. `WorkLeafController` scopes automatic review after a patch agent reports done to the
342:patch agent that produced the provisional commit; explicit review commands use the history-wide
343:review target lookup.
344:
345:`src/linearize.rs::LinearizePlanner<B>` prepares linearization questions and launches a linearizer
346:agent with decisions, groups, and required tests. `LinearizeAction`, `LinearizeGroup`,
347:`LinearizePlan`, `LinearizeQuestion`, `LinearizeHandoff`, and `LinearizeError` are the public
348:linearization workflow types. `CommandChat` and `WorkLeafController` launch linearization from the
349:exact commits recorded as reviewed in the current command-chat or controller instance; unrelated
350:historical agent metadata commits are outside the linearizer scope unless the user explicitly reviews
351:or adds them in that session. When one patch-agent id completes multiple reviewed commits in one
352:active instance, each reviewed hash is listed independently for the linearizer.
353:
354:`src/instructions.rs` is crate-private. It loads project instruction files used by `PromptPolicy`
355:for agent launch prompts.
356:
357:`src/chat_title.rs` is crate-private. It builds the prompt used for hidden chat-title backend
358:launches, sanitizes title replies to lowercase hyphenated names capped at 80 characters, provides a
359:first-prompt fallback, and tracks which sessions have already requested a generated title.
360:
361:## Extension Rules
362:
363:New UI support follows this path:
364:
365:1. Construct a `CommandChat<B>` with the desired backend.
366:2. Wrap it in `WorkLeafController<B>`.
367:3. Render from `WorkLeafSnapshot` and `WorkLeafSession`.
368:4. Drive user actions through controller methods.
369:5. Consume `WorkLeafEvent` values from `drain_events`.
370:
371:Out-of-process UI support uses `HttpControllerClient` against a running `HttpControllerServer` and
372:the same snapshot, session, and event DTOs. The HTTP transport remains an adapter over
373:`WorkLeafController`; new workflow behavior still belongs in the owning workflow or controller
374:module.
375:
376:New agent-provider support follows this path:
377:
378:1. Define an `AgentProfile` with `AgentKind::External`.
379:2. Implement `AgentBackend` for the provider.
380:3. Override streaming methods when the provider can emit real-time output.
381:4. Return an `AgentShutdownHandle` when the provider owns child processes.
382:5. Pass the profile through `CommandChat::with_agent_profile`.
383:6. Use `WorkLeafController` or `CommandChat` without modifying terminal UI code.
384:
385:New core workflow behavior belongs in the workflow module that owns the behavior. UI adapters should
386:only translate user input into controller calls and render controller snapshots. Agent providers
387:should only implement launch, send, streaming, and shutdown behavior.
388:
389:## API and Architecture Change Policy
390:
391:A breaking public API change requires human authorization before implementation. Public API includes
392:top-level re-exports in `src/lib.rs`, public items in public modules, and the documented integration
393:surfaces for UIs, agent providers, command orchestration, and core workflows. In Rust, removing or
394:renaming public items, changing public method signatures, adding required trait methods, changing
395:public enum matching behavior, changing public struct construction behavior, or changing documented
396:semantics can be breaking.
397:
398:A non-breaking public API extension does not require human authorization, but this document must
399:describe the resulting public surface whenever the extension affects UI integration, agent-provider
400:integration, command orchestration, or core workflow integration.
401:
402:An architecture change requires human authorization before implementation when the requested work can
403:only be completed by changing documented ownership, dependency direction, extension boundaries, or
404:integration paths. After authorization, this document must describe the resulting architecture in the
405:same patch as the code change.
406:
407:When compatibility is unclear, treat the change as breaking until the caller confirms otherwise.
408:
409:## Validation Expectations
410:
411:Provider-interface changes should have tests that prove an external provider can implement
412:`AgentBackend` without depending on Codex-specific code. `tests/agent_provider_interface.rs` covers
413:that contract.
414:
415:Controller and UI behavior should use `WorkLeafController`, `TerminalApp`, and `UiHarness` tests
416:instead of duplicating internal terminal or worker logic. Terminal UI behavior is covered through
417:`tests/ui_harness.rs`, `tests/terminal_ui.rs`, and `tests/terminal_app.rs`.
418:
419:The CLI/daemon transport is covered by `tests/http_orchestrator.rs`, which starts the real
420:`work-leaf-orchestrator` binary and drives it through `HttpControllerClient`. The release launcher is
421:covered by `tests/start_script.rs`, which runs the root `start` script through a pseudo-terminal with
422:prebuilt test binaries.
423:
424:Core workflow changes should test the owning module and the integration path that consumes it. The
425:existing test suites under `tests/orchestrator_protocol.rs`, `tests/patching.rs`,
426:`tests/reviews.rs`, `tests/linearize.rs`, and `tests/workspace.rs` provide the current coverage
